newsitem.title: INDIA: India says 1997/98 wheat imports may fall.
newsitem.headline: India says 1997/98 wheat imports may fall.

text.p: India is likely to import less wheat in 1997/98 (April-March) than anticipated because of sizeable government purchases from local farmers, Food Minister Raghuvansh Prasad Singh said on Thursday.
India had decided to import two million tonnes of wheat in both 1996/97 and 1997/98 to increase supplies, Singh said in a speech prepared for delivery to the International Grains Council in London.
"However, during the current year 1997/98, procurement of wheat for the central pool has almost touched nine million tonnes and is expected to go up further," he said.
"Under this scenario, there is every possibility that the quantum of imports may be reduced," he said without elaborating.
The government buys wheat from local farmers to build up buffer stocks, which it then uses to control prices by releasing stocks through a state-run distribution system.

In 1996/97 (April-March), the government bought eight million tonnes of wheat from local farmers. In March, the government said it expected to procure about 10 million tonnes in 1997/98, more than expected earlier.
Since December 1996, India has contracted to import about 2.75 million tonnes of wheat from Australia, Canada and Argentina.
In the 1996/97 (July-June) crop year, India is expected to produce 64.66 million tonnes of wheat, up from 62.62 million in the previous year.
